articles.title: German Inflation Highest Since December 2023
articles.expand: Germany's consumer price inflation accelerated for a third month in September to reach its highest level in nearly three years on the back of a surge in energy prices, yet the European Central Bank is likely to seek more evidence to establish second-round effects of the fuel price shock on the real economy before raising interest rates again.

articles.title: Trump calls for Powell to resign over Fed renovation, asks attorney general to review report
articles.expand: In a TruthSocial post, Donald Trump is calling for Jerome Powell to resign from the Fed Board over alleged mismanagement and cost overruns in the Federal Reserve headquarters renovation. He says he has asked Attorney General Todd Blanche to review an inspector general’s report and determine what action to take. Trump cites a projected cost of at least $2.5 billion and alleged shortcomings in cost estimates and construction safeguards. He threatens a government lawsuit if Powell does not resign. His suggestion that costs could reach $3.5–$4 billion is his own forecast. Analysis: Trump is turnin...

articles.title: Trump: US has almost total control of the Strait of Hormuz
articles.expand: Comments from US President Trump on Iran and the Strait of Hormuz: US has almost total control of the Strait of Hormuz. articles.title: WTI set for monthly gain amid US-Iran stalemate
articles.expand: West Texas Intermediate (WTI) Oil rebounds on Wednesday and remains on track for a monthly gain of around 5.5%. The lack of progress in US-Iran negotiations to reopen the Strait of Hormuz keeps geopolitical risks elevated, even as Middle East supply conditions improve.

articles.title: Goldman Sachs moves its call for the next Fed rate hike to December from October
articles.expand: Goldman Sachs has changed its forecast for the next Fed rate hike from October to December. Yesterday, John Williams, the New York Fed president and a permanent FOMC voter, said one more rate hike this year may be enough, provided the economy develops as expected. However, he sees “no need for urgency” after September’s hike, giving the Fed time to review more data before acting again. His outlook includes: Growth: GDP rising 2.25% this year, with economic momentum strong and potentially strengthening. Employment: Unemployment at 4% during 2027. articles.title: Per Jansson in London on the economic situation
articles.expand: Last week, the Executive Board left the policy rate unchanged at 1.75 per cent and signalled that if the outlook for inflation and economic activity remains unchanged, it is expected that increases to the rate will begin this year. In London, Deputy Governor Per Jansson spoke at Nordea and the Swedish Chamber of Commerce for the United Kingdom about the economic situation and his reasoning behind the decision.

articles.title: Australia Inflation Rises In August
articles.expand: Australia's consumer price inflation accelerated in August on higher housing and transport costs, the Australian Bureau of Statistics said Wednesday. Consumer price inflation rose to 4.0 percent from 3.5 percent in July. Inflation continues to remain above the central bank target range of 2-3 percent.
